On this page

Configuration ​

Saidi resolves every configurable value through one precedence chain: genuine environment → the settings/secrets store → .env → a built-in default. This page lists what lives where, the real keys and defaults, and which changes need a restart.

Where configuration lives on disk ​

Two directories matter, and they are deliberately different things.

ROOT is process.cwd() — the installed package or source checkout. The CLI (bin/saidi.js) chdirs here before spawning the server. Only package-relative assets are read from it: .env, the built client (client/dist), and the registry's "don't register Saidi's own repo" guard.

DATA_DIR is where persistent state lives. It must sit outside the package, because a global update (npm i -g …) rewrites the package directory. Resolution, highest first:

OrderSourceResult
1SAIDI_HOMEpath.resolve(SAIDI_HOME)
2SAIDI_DEV setROOT — a source checkout keeps state repo-local
3default~/.saidi (via os.homedir())

Derived paths:

DATA_DIR/
├── config/        # settings.json (legacy/migration input; bind values read by the CLI)
├── memory/        # secrets.json (local-no-Mongo fallback), runs, memory files
└── agents/        # custom agent definitions (AGENT.md dirs, skills, mcp.json)

In cloud mode each organisation is nested one level down — DATA_DIR/orgs/<orgId>/ with its own memory/, agents/, config/, and repos/. Local mode returns the flat paths above unchanged, so existing installs need no migration.

SAIDI_HOME and SAIDI_DEV are genuine-env only

DATA_DIR is resolved at module load, before .env is parsed. A line in .env for SAIDI_HOME does nothing — export it in the shell or set it in the container. (SAIDI_DEV is split: the data-dir half is genuine-only, but the dev-frontend redirect is read from .env at runtime, and any value — even "0" — counts as on.)

Precedence ​

resolvePrecedence() in src/orchestrator/config.ts is the single place the rule lives:

  1. Genuine environment — a variable the real OS/container/shell set before .env or the store loaded. Captured as a snapshot at module load, so later process.env mutations cannot erase the distinction. A container override is deliberate and always wins.
  2. The store — MongoDB-backed system settings and secrets (what the Settings UI writes). It must win over .env, otherwise a value you set in the UI is silently shadowed by a stale .env line.
  3. .env — a dev convenience only, read from ROOT/.env.
  4. The built-in default.

Empty or whitespace-only values are treated as absent at every layer.

The settings store ​

System settings are platform-global and live as one MongoDB document (SystemSettingsModel, _id system). initSettings() hydrates an in-process cache at boot; reads are synchronous off that cache; writes go through to Mongo. Mongo is required — initSettings() throws without a live connection, and updateSystemSettings() refuses to persist.

config/settings.json is the legacy file: migrateLegacySettingsToMongo() folds it in once (Mongo values win, missing legacy keys fill in), and bin/saidi.js still reads port and host from it to decide which URL to open. A partial file is fine — every missing key falls back to its default:

json
{
  "primeModel": "",
  "defaultBranchMode": "new",
  "defaultApproval": "auto",
  "cronTickSeconds": 30,
  "textProvider": "claude",
  "openaiRealtimeModel": "gpt-realtime-mini",
  "openaiRealtimeVoice": "marin"
}

Every value is passed through sanitize() on load and on write: an unknown, out-of-range, or garbage value silently falls back to the default rather than being stored.

Pricing ​

Rates are USD per 1M tokens. 0 means unpriced — costUsd stays 0 unless the SDK itself reports a cost. A negative or non-numeric value falls back rather than pricing spend at a nonsense figure. Cache reads bill at 10% of input.

KeyTypeDefaultWhat it does
customPriceIn / customPriceOutnumber ≥00Custom-endpoint token prices
voicePriceTextIn / voicePriceAudioInnumber ≥00Realtime input rates — the browser holds the WebRTC leg, so the turn reports its own counts and these convert them
voicePriceTextOut / voicePriceAudioOutnumber ≥00Realtime output rates; audio and text are separate because realtime audio costs an order of magnitude more per token
creditsMarginnumber ≥11Multiplier applied to costUsd when debiting the wallet; 1 = at cost
creditsEnforcebooleanfalsePersisted and validated, but no production code path reads it. Wallet enforcement keys off cloud mode instead — see Credits, Usage & Spend Limits. Setting it has no effect today.
runCostAlertUsdnumber ≥00Emit a run.cost_exceeded reflex event once a run's cumulative cost crosses this; 0 = off

Runs and execution ​

KeyTypeDefaultWhat it does
defaultExecutionModeguided | autonomousautonomousExecution mode stamped onto new runs
defaultEffortlow | medium | highmediumDefault effort mode; the run composer can override per run
defaultBranchModenew | currentnewFallback policy for a project that declares none
defaultApprovalconfirm | autoconfirmFallback approval policy for a project that declares none
requirePlanApprovalbooleanfalsePark a guided run for plan approval before any task runs
verifyTasksbooleanfalseCheck a completed task against its acceptance criteria before it may be marked done. Guided runs always verify; this adds it to autonomous ones
optimizationModeoff | shadow | canary | oncanaryRollout gate for optimizations that may discard worker context or skip a command
runWorktreesbooleantrueGive each run its own git worktree per project instead of sharing the repo's working tree
routeReadOnlyCheapbooleantrueRoute read-only delegate_to_project mode:'ask' delegations to the cheap tier
autoLearnPreferencesbooleantrueObserve operator corrections and store scoped, inspectable memory records
cronTickSecondsnumber ≥560Cron scheduler sweep interval

Guards and limits ​

Guard thresholds are clamped to 1…50; a value below 1 would refuse the first attempt, so garbage falls back to the default instead of disarming the guard.

KeyTypeDefaultWhat it does
maxTaskAttemptsinteger 1–503Attempts one checklist task gets before the runtime escalates. A task may lower this via attemptBudget; nothing may raise it
maxSameTaskDispatchesinteger 1–503Dispatches of the same (target, task) before the runtime refuses to repeat it
maxDelegationFailsinteger 1–503Consecutive failures for one target before it leaves rotation for the rest of the run; any success resets it
turnMaxStepsinteger ≥080Hard cap on agentic steps in a single PRIME turn (SDK maxTurns); 0 = off
turnMaxCostUsdnumber ≥05Hard USD ceiling for a single PRIME turn (SDK maxBudgetUsd); 0 = off
delegationTimeoutMinutesinteger ≥020Wall-clock ceiling for one delegation; the delegation is aborted and reported as a timeout while the run continues. 0 = off

Context and sessions ​

Auto-compact windows are clamped to 20_000…2_000_000 tokens.

KeyTypeDefaultWhat it does
primeAutoCompactWindowinteger200000Auto-compact PRIME's main-chat session as it approaches this many tokens
workerAutoCompactWindowinteger200000Same, for a delegated agent worker's session
delegationResultCapinteger ≥5008000Max characters of a delegation result that enter PRIME's main-chat context — that context is replayed every future turn
memoryInjectCapinteger ≥10006000Max characters of a memory file sent whole into a worker's task; a larger one is filtered to the facts relevant to the task
sessionPerTaskbooleanfalseStart a fresh agent session at each checklist-task boundary instead of resuming one across the run
adaptiveSessionsbooleantrueReset a participant at a real task boundary once its context crosses the threshold; same-task retries always retain their session
adaptiveSessionThresholdinteger120000The context size that triggers an adaptive reset

Updates and approvals ​

KeyTypeDefaultWhat it does
autoUpdatebooleantrueInstall updates and restart once no run is active. Ignored in cloud mode, source checkouts, and unsupervised starts
autoApproveobject of booleansall falsePer-action grants that skip a management tool's confirm card; the permission gate still applies

autoApprove accepts only these keys — anything else is dropped, and any non-true value becomes false:

create_agent · remove_agent
add_skill · import_skill
add_mcp_server · remove_mcp_server
add_project · remove_project · sync_projects
delete_cron · delete_reflex

Sandbox ​

VariableDefaultWhat it does
SAIDI_SANDBOXunset1 runs agent workers inside the Docker sandbox
SAIDI_SANDBOX_IMAGEsaidi-sandbox:latestImage tag the pool launches
SAIDI_SANDBOX_MEMORY2gPer-container memory limit
SAIDI_SANDBOX_CPUS2Per-container CPU limit
SAIDI_SANDBOX_NETWORKbridgeSet to host for host networking

With the sandbox off, agents run in-host; the env allow-list still withholds host secrets, but cross-org filesystem isolation needs the sandbox. If it is enabled and either the Docker daemon is unreachable or the image is missing, boot warns and Claude delegations fail until it is fixed.

VariableDefaultWhat it does

SAIDI_MAIL_FROMSaidi <noreply@localhost>From address for outbound mail
SAIDI_RESEND_API_KEY''Required when the driver is resend

Webhooks ​

The five fixed sources are store-backed (see below). Any additional source is configured directly by name — SAIDI_WEBHOOK_<NAME>_SCHEME (bearer | hmac | none), _SECRET, _HEADER (default x-signature), _PREFIX (default sha256=), _ENCODING (hex | base64, default hex), and _VERIFY_TOKEN. Non-alphanumeric characters in the source name become underscores.

Marketplace server ​

The marketplace runs as its own process (saidi-marketplace) with its own variables: MARKETPLACE_PORT (default 8787), MARKETPLACE_HOST (127.0.0.1), MARKETPLACE_MONGODB_URI (mongodb://127.0.0.1:27017/saidi_marketplace), MARKETPLACE_PUBLIC_URL (http://localhost:<port>), MARKETPLACE_ADMIN_TOKEN, MARKETPLACE_IP_SALT (saidi-marketplace), MARKETPLACE_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID / MARKETPLACE_GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET, and MARKETPLACE_SEED (set to 0 to skip seeding).

Secrets ​

Credentials are a separate store: one global MongoDB document, encrypted at rest with envelope AES-256-GCM under SAIDI_MASTER_KEY whenever that key is set. Cloud mode requires the key; local mode keeps it optional and stores the document plaintext, the same trust level as the gitignored memory/secrets.json it replaced. Cloud never writes secrets to disk.

Each field maps to the environment variable the SDKs actually read, and hydrateEnvFromSecrets() pushes the resolved value into process.env at boot so the app runs with no .env while a container override still wins:

FieldEnvironment variable
mongodbUriMONGODB_URI
anthropicModelANTHROPIC_MODEL
anthropicBaseUrlANTHROPIC_BASE_URL
anthropicApiKeyANTHROPIC_API_KEY
anthropicAuthTokenANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN
claudeCodeOauthTokenCLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN
openaiApiKeyOPENAI_API_KEY
saidiGithubTokenSAIDI_GITHUB_TOKEN
webhookGenericTokenSAIDI_WEBHOOK_GENERIC_TOKEN
webhookGithubSecretSAIDI_WEBHOOK_GITHUB_SECRET
webhookStripeSecretSAIDI_WEBHOOK_STRIPE_SECRET
webhookMetaSecretSAIDI_WEBHOOK_META_SECRET
webhookMetaVerifyTokenSAIDI_WEBHOOK_META_VERIFY_TOKEN

MONGODB_URI is the one exception: it is bootstrap config — how the process reaches Mongo — so it is never persisted to Mongo and resolves from genuine env or .env only.

Model provider configuration ​

modelProvider is one choice that routes the whole system, and applyModelProviderEnv() makes it real by pinning the ambient Anthropic variables every Claude SDK call reads:

modelProviderSetUnset
customANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, ANTHROPIC_MODEL = customModel, and every family alias = customModelANTHROPIC_API_KEY, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN
anthropicANTHROPIC_API_KEY, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, ANTHROPIC_MODELANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, all family aliases

The family aliases are ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL, ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL, ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL, ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_FABLE_MODEL, and ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL. They exist because ANTHROPIC_MODEL only sets the session default — a nested sub-agent that asks for sonnet or opus by family would otherwise request an Anthropic model id from an endpoint that serves only its own.

This override beats a genuine env var

applyModelProviderEnv() deliberately overwrites even a real container environment value for those variables. Picking a provider in Settings is an explicit instruction about which endpoint to use, and a half-applied mix (custom base URL plus official key) is worse than either. Set a custom endpoint in Settings, not as ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL in your compose file.

Ports and hosts ​

getPort() and getHost() resolve genuine env → the store → .env → default. The port is validated at every layer: a value that is not an integer in 1…65535 is skipped and the next layer is tried, ending at 4317. The host defaults to 127.0.0.1 — localhost only.

bash
# Bind to all interfaces on a non-default port for this process only
HOST=0.0.0.0 PORT=8080 npm start

Bind settings are injected into the config module from the hydrated settings cache immediately before listen(), so a value saved in Settings is what the next boot binds to.

The saidi CLI reads port and host from config/settings.json directly (with env still winning) so it can wait for the socket and open the right browser URL without importing server config. When SAIDI_DEV is on, the one app URL is the Vite dev server at :5317; this process is only the API and WebSocket origin its proxy forwards to.

Database and storage ​

MongoDB is required. There is deliberately no degraded file-backed mode and no background late-connect path.

  • Server — from resolveSecret('mongodbUri'), falling back to mongodb://127.0.0.1:27017. Host, credentials, and options all come from here.
  • Database name — derived from SAIDI_CLOUD: saidi_cloud when 1, otherwise saidi. withDatabase() replaces whatever database the configured URI carries, so one stored server serves both modes. Do not put a database name in the URI.
  • Connect timeout — serverSelectionTimeoutMS: 2500.
  • Failure — a failed connect at boot is fatal (exit 1). A later disconnected event terminates the process after a 1s grace period rather than accepting non-durable changes; a supervisor restarts it so every in-memory working set is rebuilt from the authoritative snapshot.

Structured records (runs, activity, settings, secrets, channel config) live in Mongo. Human-editable markdown memory and the scanned project registry stay as files, mirrored under memory/, because they are meant to be inspected and edited on disk. See Runs for what a run persists.

Changing configuration safely ​

Takes effect immediately. Anything read through getSystemSettings() on each use — guards, caps, execution defaults, approval toggles. updateSystemSettings() merges, sanitizes, replaces the in-process cache, and writes through to Mongo. The settings route also calls applyModelProviderEnv() on every save, so a provider or custom-model change applies to the next call without a restart.

Needs a fresh boot. A new MONGODB_URI (the Mongoose connection is opened once at startup), re-hydrating env from the secret store, reloading the agent catalog after an import, and a changed host/port (they persist to Mongo but only bind on the next listen()).

Rather than asking you to restart by hand, those routes call requestRestart() after the response is flushed. The process exits with code 75 and the supervisor in bin/saidi.js relaunches it — the old child fully exits first, so the port is released before the new one binds. The auto-update path uses code 76, which tells the supervisor to run the global install between spawns (npm i -g rewrites the very directory the process executes from).

Self-restart only works under the supervisor

requestRestart() is a no-op returning false unless SAIDI_SUPERVISED=1. Started directly with npm start or node dist/server.js, nothing would bring the process back, so the route reports that you must restart manually. The settings save response includes a restarting flag so you can tell which happened.

Shutdown is graceful in both paths: channels and the reflex engine stop, sandbox containers are disposed, dashboard WebSockets are force-closed first (a long-lived /ws socket would otherwise hang server.close()), then debounced activity and run writes are drained before the Mongo connection drops.

Verifying what actually resolved ​

The server prints a resolved-configuration summary at boot — mode and paths, the bind URL, the redacted Mongo URI, the active model provider, voice settings, cloud auth (in cloud mode), sandbox and supervision state, and mail/webhook credentials. Each row is tagged with where the value came from: shell env, store, .env, or default. Secrets are masked to their last three characters and connection URIs have credentials redacted.

Start there when a value is not what you expect — it turns the precedence rules into something you can read instead of guess.
